answer: A sequential work-history check stops Sybil attacks by making each identity earn standing over time, not at signup. A new account starts in a harbor with no voting weight and must complete time-gated, verified tasks, each sealed with a cipher proving the work was done in order and cannot be replayed for another account. Those tasks form a bridge to trusted status, unlocked only after sustained, distinct work. An attacker cannot clone one identity into thousands for free: every fake account must pay the same weeks of sequential work, so Sybils scale linearly in time and effort.
